tickets.summary: K-3401 NDE vibration rose from 2.1 to 4.6 mm/s over six weeks and remains below alarm but is still rising; loss of this sole gas export compressor would force recycle and cut production within an hour.
tickets.recommended_action: Rotating equipment specialist today: diagnose NDE vibration, set operating/repair disposition; correct per findings and verify vibration against approved limits. Continue daily trending. Obtain source-required attention today. Verify trend, limits and vibration cause.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is main gas export compression. NDE bearing vibration more than doubled over six weeks and has not plateaued, supporting strong progression. Remaining below alarm limits the assessment; neither imminent loss nor an actual compression failure is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of this single export compressor would put the platform into recycle and cut production within an hour, with no spare or workaround. This supports a material operational consequence; the supplied evidence does not establish the scale or severe exposure needed for a higher band.

tickets.recommended_action: Have integrity engineer investigate passing, set operating/repair disposition and regulatory deadline; repair or replace if confirmed. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Test relief function and seat tightness. Check local gas levels and personnel exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Hissing and hydrocarbon smell while operating pressure is well below set pressure indicate a meaningful precursor consistent with passing. This supports active degradation, but neither progression nor inability to relieve overpressure is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of this nonredundant relief function would remove overpressure protection from the first-stage production separator, creating a specific severe pressure-boundary failure and hydrocarbon-release path. Actual demand conditions and personnel exposure are unknown; extreme consequence scale is not established.

tickets.summary: FW-8102 failed its first start, then started on attempt 2 after about 8 s cranking and reached rated pressure; 22.8 V at rest raises starting-system concerns for firewater on demand, while FW-8101 later delivered 9.2 versus 11 barg design.
tickets.recommended_action: Firewater engineer: set operating/repair disposition; correct proven faults; retain weekly tests. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Test batteries/charger and starting air. Verify A pressure/flow and duty capacity. Retest B first-start and rated pressure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is FW-8102 starting on demand to supply firewater. Its first-attempt failure directly demonstrates interrupted required function. The successful second attempt after about eight seconds of cranking and subsequent rated pressure bound the failure but do not erase it. The 22.8 V measurement was at rest, not during cranking; battery or starting-air causation remains unconfirmed.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure to start removes this pump's on-demand firewater contribution, compromising fire protection against a major-accident scenario. Full redundancy credit is unsupported: the explicitly linked partner started successfully on 17 June but delivered 9.2 barg against 11 barg design, with flow unmeasured. This does not establish that both pumps are unavailable or that required system capacity is insufficient. Production shutdown is the stated consequence if both become unavailable; extreme consequences are not established.

tickets.summary: PL-1002 window 2 near the low-point drain has wet-insulation corrosion: 6.2 mm versus 7.4 mm minimum, threatening full-wellhead-pressure hydrocarbon containment; adjacent windows remain within tolerance.
tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer to set operating/repair disposition; replace wet insulation, stop water ingress and approve metal repair/replacement; verify restored containment against 7.4 mm minimum. Map wall loss and verify current containment. Check release inventory and personnel exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is pressure containment by PL-1002. Wall thickness below the stated minimum, heavy scaling and saturated insulation establish advanced damage with an active corrosion mechanism, supporting the 7–8 band. Adjacent acceptable windows limit the demonstrated extent, not the local defect. Neither imminent rupture nor actual containment loss is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of this six-inch production flowline's containment would release hydrocarbons at full wellhead pressure, providing a specific severe pressure-release and potential ignition/injury path. No redundant line is recorded. This supports the severe band, but release inventory, isolation performance and personnel exposure are insufficiently defined to support extreme consequences.

The linked June 22 V-1201 observation concerns another item and proves neither shared damage nor restoration. tickets.summary: FG-0455 failed hydrocarbon detection at 50 percent LEL with both cylinders; two responding heads retain 2oo3 capability, but compression-module gas protection has lost its failure margin.
tickets.recommended_action: Instrument engineer to diagnose head/signal path and approve repair or replacement and operating controls. Check impairment/deviation register. Retest head/group with 50 percent LEL gas. Verify current group/control status.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed component is the individual detector head, required to respond to hydrocarbon gas. No response on the first test or repeat with a second cylinder confirms function loss, despite clean-looking optics. The two responding partner heads moderate impact, not this head's likelihood.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of this hydrocarbon-detection head materially degrades compression-module protection. Both other heads responded correctly, supporting retained voted capability rather than total defeat. The arrangement has lost failure tolerance; supplied guidance supports moderate rather than extreme impact.

tickets.summary: P-3305's third low-pressure trip this month has left manifold inhibitor injection intermittent for around ten days; production continues, but inhibitor starvation threatens downstream carbon steel corrosion within weeks.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect diaphragm and low-pressure trip cause; repair per mechanical engineer disposition and verify sustained manifold dosing at required rate and pressure. Confirm repair and current injection status. Integrity engineer: assess missed-dose damage.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The required function is sustained corrosion-inhibitor injection to the wellhead manifold. impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of inhibitor injection creates a specifically supported delayed integrity threat: downstream carbon steel starts corroding within weeks, with consequences appearing months later. tickets.summary: DEL-8300 failed spray coverage at ~12/60 north-quadrant nozzles above two producing wellheads despite normal header flow, weakening fire protection. A later closed valve was reopened; closure duration and coverage restoration remain unknown.
tickets.recommended_action: Fire-protection engineer: inspect branches/nozzles, clear blockage and approve disposition. Verify current protection control alignment. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Witness function test; close impairment only after pass. Check wellhead exposure and safeguards.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is delivery of effective deluge spray coverage over the north-quadrant wellheads. The full-flow test demonstrated failed delivery at approximately 12 of 60 nozzles, establishing partial required-function loss rather than merely a deterioration precursor. Normal header conditions do not establish local coverage. Later valve reopening does not demonstrate restoration or explain the earlier test.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of effective deluge coverage directly above two producing wellheads compromises fire protection and provides a specific severe fire-escalation and personnel-exposure path. No redundant deluge arrangement is recorded. Remaining nozzle delivery limits the demonstrated extent, but does not establish adequate protection. Extreme installation-wide consequences are not established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of this survival craft removes evacuation capacity needed for personnel escape, a specific severe safety consequence path. tickets.recommended_action: Instrument engineer to diagnose drift, correct as found and prove calibration, control and alarm to approved limits. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Verify both legs and control alignment. Verify level-loss consequences and safeguards.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is providing reliable interface-level input to control and the high-level alarm. Steadily increasing divergence over about three weeks supports strong progression. Absolute accuracy and acceptance limits remain unverified, so confirmed function loss is not established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of reliable input affects separator level control and the high-level alarm, supporting material operational consequences. The backup's later noncredible flat-line observation prevents crediting capable redundancy without verification. No specific severe consequence path is established; neither vessel deterioration nor total separator loss is inferred.

tickets.summary: V-1305's partly detached inlet deflector threatens well-testing performance: one of four brackets has corroded through. It is out of service, with sound shell and heads, and can be bypassed without production impact.
tickets.recommended_action: Plan next-shutdown inspection of all deflector supports; replace corroded bracket and resecure plate to integrity-engineer-approved design, with engineering acceptance before reuse. Verify inlet deflection before reuse.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Assessed function is inlet deflection within the test separator. Partial detachment is a credible precursor to loss of that function, but operational failure is unproven. The confirmed out-of-service observation and absence of a production requirement limit near-term demand; progression and remaining support capacity are unmeasured.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of inlet deflection could impair the localized well-testing function. The separator is out of service, its shell and heads are sound, and indefinite isolation/bypass has no production impact. Total pressure-boundary failure or a current protection loss is not the supported failure path.

tickets.summary: FW-8101 started correctly but delivered 9.2 barg versus 11 barg design, with flow unmeasured: firewater protection impairment is suspected, not confirmed. Partner FW-8102's earlier first-attempt start failure leaves backup reliability unresolved.
tickets.recommended_action: Firewater engineer to direct operating/repair disposition and correct confirmed faults; retain weekly tests. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Retest flow/pressure against approved duty. Inspect test-line valves and pump wear. Verify FW-8102 duty and fire/personnel coverage.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Assessed function is pump A's required firewater delivery, not starting. Pressure stabilised below design despite correct first-time starting and normal engine parameters, a meaningful performance precursor. Unmeasured flow and unknown acceptance criteria prevent confirmation of required-duty failure; wear and test-line restriction remain alternative suspected causes.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of required firewater delivery could compromise fire suppression and expose personnel to fire escalation. The explicit partner cannot be credited as fully reliable: on 3 June it failed its first start, then started on the second attempt after about eight seconds of cranking and achieved rated discharge pressure. This supports a severe protection-consequence path, not confirmed total firewater loss or extreme consequences. Both pumps being unavailable would require production shutdown.

tickets.summary: Loose, wind-flapping cladding on K-3401's second-stage discharge line risks falling and injuring personnel; no process concern is reported, but personnel exposure remains unknown.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect cladding and adjacent fixings; resecure loose lagging/cladding to a maintenance-engineer-approved repair and verify secure retention afterward. Check mass, fall height and personnel access.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is secure retention of the discharge-line cladding, not gas compression. Loose lagging and wind-flapping cladding establish advanced deterioration with a stated dropped-object trajectory, but detachment has not been established. The June 2 bearing-vibration observation is a separate mechanism from this June 19 finding and is not transferred into this assessment.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of cladding retention has a credible dropped-object personnel-injury path, supporting material personnel consequence rather than housekeeping alone. Mass, fall height and occupancy are unknown, so a severe consequence band is unsupported. The explicit absence of process concern excludes attributing compressor trip and production loss to this defect.

tickets.summary: DEL-8300's north-quadrant valve blocked deluge protection above two producing wellheads for an unknown duration without a logged impairment; it was reopened, but restored coverage remains unverified.
tickets.recommended_action: Fire protection engineer: fit status tag and approve corrective disposition. Verify current protection control alignment. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Witness function test; close impairment only after pass. Investigate closure/duration. Verify wellhead fire exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is delivery of deluge through the north-quadrant branch. The chained-closed isolation valve establishes actual loss of that function when discovered. Immediate reopening is confirmed, but restored delivery is not; this is not a claim that the valve remains closed.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of north-quadrant deluge removes local fire protection above two producing wellheads, providing a specific escalation and personnel-harm path. No redundant arrangement is listed. This supports severe consequences, not an assumed total-platform loss or an extreme consequence score.

tickets.summary: Damp insulation and rust runoff at V-1201's manway suggest concealed corrosion threatening first-stage pressure containment; wall condition is unknown, and boundary failure could release process fluids and interrupt production.
tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer to set operating/repair disposition, address moisture and confirmed damage, and verify containment to approved criteria. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Strip insulation; map corrosion by visual/UT. Check local inventory and personnel exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Assessed function is first-stage pressure containment. Damp insulation and rust runoff are meaningful precursors to concealed corrosion, but wall loss, progression and leakage remain unverified. Historical thick-wall construction moderates likelihood without establishing remaining margin. Linked pipework, transmitter and PSV observations do not establish vessel damage.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the entire first-stage pressure boundary provides a specific severe process-containment consequence, with potential personnel exposure and interruption of first-stage production. No redundant vessel is recorded. Inventory, operating conditions and exposure are insufficient to support an extreme consequence score; the actual effectiveness of linked relief protection is not established by its earlier observation.
